title: Can you buy gift cards with a credit card?

asr.full_text: Hey WalletHubbers! A lot of people ask whether you can buy gift cards with a credit card, and the short answer is yes, but not as straightforward as you might think, so let me go over some basic tips to keep in mind along the way. First of all, it's important to note that while you can buy gift cards with a credit card, it won't work everywhere. Some retailers will accept credit card payments, others won't. On that note, stores' payment policies change from time to time, but some major retailers, where you can generally buy gift cards with a credit card, include Amazon, Target, Walmart, Home Depot, Walgreens, and CVS. On the flip side, some stores where you probably can't buy gift cards with a credit card include Giant, SaveMart, and Harris Teeter. One of the main reasons why some stores don't let you buy gift cards with a credit card is the risk of fraud. Buying gift cards with counterfeit or stolen credit cards is actually a common practice, and some stores are actually a lot more confident in their fraud prevention capabilities than others, but as more stores update their credit card security measures, you'll probably see more and more places that let you buy gift cards with a credit card. Still, it's always good to ask in-store before checking out so you don't end up being surprised. One other thing that may not let you earn rewards for gift card purchases are things that you should add to your credit card store wallet, such as your credit card vouch mentioning is your credit card issuer may or may not let you earn rewards for gift card purchases. For example, gift cards aren't eligible for rewards on American Express cards, but if such a restriction exists, it should be listed in the card's terms. If you do earn rewards for gift card purchases, be careful. If it seems like you're trying to game the system by purchasing gift cards just to meet the spending requirements for a rewards bonus or to earn more than your fair share in ongoing rewards, your credit card company could close your account due to suspected rewards abuse. On the other hand, many credit card rewards programs allow cardholders to redeem points for Miles or her gift cards. That's another legit way to get gift cards with your credit card. Now that you know the ins and outs of buying gift cards with a credit card, it's time to make sure you have the right credit card for gift card shopping. You can check out WalletHub's latest picks by clicking the button here. Best of luck, WalletHubbers!
